newsitem.title: FRANCE: French leftists line up for vote victory spoils.
newsitem.headline: French leftists line up for vote victory spoils.

text.p: Top leftist and ecologist allies scrambled on Tuesday for the spoils of their election victory as new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin prepared to announce his cabinet choices on Wednesday.

Most of the jockeying went on behind the scenes, but women were the most forthcoming. Greens leader Dominique Voynet said she sought several cabinet posts for her party -- a broad ministry including the environment and a junior ministry for social affairs or women's rights.

Former environment minister Segolene Royal openly bid to become speaker of the National Assembly, challenging fellow Socialist and former prime minister Laurent Fabius who was widely believed to be the frontrunner for the job -- which he has held before.

"Yes I am a candidate. It seems entirely legitimate to me that there should be several Socialist candidates for the assembly presidency," said Royal, 44, a close Jospin adviser and frequent Socialist spokeswoman during the party's successful parliamentary election campaign.

Fabius is believed to be out of the running for Jospin's cabinet because he is under judicial investigation in connection with the 1980s distribution, at a time when he was prime minister, of AIDS-tainted blood products that killed hundreds of haemophiliacs.
Jospin has said he will continue a policy of the previous centre-right government barring individuals who are under investigation from cabinet posts.
So far, Jospin has made just two appointments, naming Olivier Schrameck as his chief of staff and Henri Pradaux as the director of his personal office.

Schrameck, 46, had been secretary general of the Constitutional Council, France's constitutional watchdog. He served as Jospin's chief of staff when Jospin was education minister under the late president Francois Mitterrand.
Pradaux, who had been director of Jospin's personal office at Socialist Party headquarters, also worked in his education ministry.
